messages:
incident-bot: Pager — SLO breach detected for streaming-proxy in eu-west. p95=450ms, p99=2.1s (SLO p99=1s). Multiple streaming stalls and TLS handshake spikes reported. Paging @sre-rotation.

sre-rotation: ack — I'm on. Adding @eli (net) and @marta (infra). Spawning triage thread here.

eli: looking at VPC flow logs and tcpdump from the streaming-proxy frontend. Seeing repeated SYN retransmits between az-a and az-b, high TCP retransmit counts, and a bunch of SNAT errors on nat-gw-3. Ephemeral port exhaustion looks likely.

marta: confirmed TLS handshake latency spike in traces — we see handshake RTTs 200–800ms in eu-west, connection setup is dominating tail. No obvious CPU or GPU pressure on model hosts.

shreyas: customer-impact note: CS is already seeing ~12 customers reporting stream stalls / reconnects. Some reports of >10s stalls. Putting a short customer update together.

netops: quick check of NAT metrics — nat-gw-3 ephemeral_port_utilization=98%, conntrack=near-limit, retransmit spikes correlate with nat-gw-3 CPU and conntrack pressure.

sre-rotation: runbook step 1: attempt graceful failover away from nat-gw-3. netops, can you re-route streaming-proxy egress to nat-gw-7 for eu-west?

netops: doing route table tweak now — updating rt-eu-west-streams to point to nat-gw-7. Command: 
```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abcd --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id nat-gw-7
```
Applying in 30s.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline paused for eu-west rolling updates due to incident flag.

eli: I pushed a temporary conntrack cleanup on nat-gw-3 to free ports (runbook safe-cleanup). Also increasing ephemeral port range on nat-gw-3 as a stopgap (`/proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range` to 10000-65535). Will monitor.

incident-bot: Telemetry update (T+4m): p99 dropped from 2.1s -> 1.2s after route change; streaming stall rate down 45%. Still above SLO.

marta: starting canary to move a subset of streaming traffic to eu-west2 dedicated pool (no cross-AZ hairpinning). Target 10% traffic shift.

eli: after reroute, flow logs show majority of egress now via nat-gw-7, retransmits fall ~70%. However DNS retries increased briefly — likely due to in-flight connections during switch. I've adjusted resolver timeouts on the proxy to reduce tail.

shreyas: CS update draft: "We’re investigating elevated streaming latency in EU. Engineers are rerouting traffic and applying mitigations; many customers’ streams have recovered. Continue monitoring. We’ll post a follow-up in 30m." @customer-success please send.

customer-success: sending now, included incident links and suggested mitigations for customers (retry/backoff tips).

support-bot: created ticket INC-2026-442 with NAT vendor — attaching SNAT logs and conntrack dumps for deep-dive.

eli: additional observation: DNS queries to internal resolvers had ~5–10% retransmits during spike window; looks like packet loss for small UDP packets when conntrack thrashes. Moving resolver to in-process local cache for streaming-proxy seems to help.

incident-bot: Telemetry update (T+18m): p99=0.95s, p95=320ms, streaming stall alerts mostly cleared, but we're keeping the page until stable for 30m.

sre-rotation: mitigation summary so far: 1) route stream egress to nat-gw-7, 2) conntrack cleanup + widen ephemeral port range on nat-gw-3, 3) start canary shift to eu-west2 dedicated pool, 4) local DNS cache for proxies.

marta: logging follow-up: we should add TLS handshake timing as a primary SLO signal (right now it's aggregated into connection latency). Filing an action item.

eli: agreed — long-term fixes: increase NAT capacity, add ephemeral port utilization alarm with automated drain, and improve conntrack cleanup logic. Also verify path MTU and packet retransmit thresholds between AZs.

shreyas: customer-impact tally: 12 customers reported intermittent reconnects, 3 customers had degraded UX for ~6–12 minutes. No data loss reported. CS has set expectation window and offered follow-up.

sre-rotation: we're moving to post-incident verification window. If no regressions in 30m, we'll close. Please file follow-up PRs for runbook changes and alert tweaks.

marta: follow-up action items: 
- add NAT ephem util alarm (critical)
- add TLS-handshake SLO alert (p95/p99)
- update streaming runbook with cross-zone NAT mitigation steps
- vendor deep-dive with packet captures attached to INC-2026-442

incident-bot: Incident state -> monitoring. p99 currently 0.83s and stable for 10m.

sre-rotation: closing the page. Thanks everyone for quick response :thumbsup: If you still see anomalies, re-open thread.

eli: will follow up with a short postmortem and remediation PRs later today.

marta: great job. Adding retro notes to ops docs. :tada:
